requirements.title: Worktree lifecycle
requirements.rationale: A per-run detached worktree lets patch application proceed without borrowing the trunk checkout and makes crash recovery a matter of deleting a directory.

criteria.condition: a rebuild reaches patch application
criteria.action: create a detached worktree with the typed WorktreeAdd call, which runs `git worktree add --detach <path> <upstream base sha>` in the trunk, where <path> is the absolute path (made absolute with filepath.Abs) <workspace_root>/<slug>/rebuild/<job id>
criteria.contract: WorktreeAdd is called once on the trunk runner; the path argument is absolute, equals filepath.Abs('ws/<slug>/rebuild/job-42'); the commit argument is the SHA returned by resolveUpstreamBase; the call is the `git worktree add --detach` form

setup: a mockGitRunner recording typed calls
a context carrying job ID 'job-42'
WorkspaceRoot is a relative path such as 'ws'
check.pseudocode: h.HandleRebuildJob(ctxWithJobID('job-42'), job); c = mock.calls('WorktreeAdd')[0]; assert filepath.IsAbs(c.path); assert c.path == abs('ws/slug/rebuild/job-42'); assert c.sha == baseSHA

criteria.condition: the job context carries no job ID or the configured WorkspaceRoot is empty
criteria.action: use a random ID in place of the job ID when the job ID is absent, and derive the worktree path from the same parent directory as the trunk path when WorkspaceRoot is empty
criteria.contract: both worktree paths are <tmp>/<slug>/rebuild/<id> with a non-empty id; the two ids differ; no error is returned because of the empty root

setup: a mockGitRunner
a context without a job ID
WorkspaceRoot is empty and the trunk path is <tmp>/<slug>/trunk
check.pseudocode: p1 = pathOf(run()); p2 = pathOf(run()); assert dir(p1) == tmp+'/slug/rebuild'; assert base(p1) != '' ; assert p1 != p2

criteria.action: build a second GitRunner with h.NewGitRunner(worktreePath) after the worktree directory exists, run log, rev-parse, cherry-pick, merge, rerere, `diff --diff-filter=U`, `commit --no-edit`, `reset --hard` to the pre-patch HEAD and worktree HEAD reads through it, and use the trunk runner only for fetch-adjacent reads, config, worktree add/remove/prune, the _rebuild_temp migration and the final ref update
criteria.contract: NewGitRunner is called with the worktree path and the directory exists at that moment; log, cherry-pick, merge, rerere, diff --diff-filter=U, commit --no-edit and HEAD reads are recorded only on the worktree runner; the trunk runner records only fetch-adjacent reads, config, worktree add/remove/prune, update-ref and rev-parse

setup: a RebuildHandler whose NewGitRunner records the path argument and whether the directory existed at call time
a mock worktree runner and a mock trunk runner each recording commands
one rebase patch and one merge patch
check.pseudocode: assert worktreeRunner.commands ⊇ {log, cherry-pick, merge}; assert trunkRunner.commands ∩ {cherry-pick, merge, log --right-only, commit} == ∅

criteria.action: for any exit path (success, conflict, transient error, early return, cancellation), remove the worktree with WorktreeRemove (`git worktree remove --force <path>`) followed by WorktreePrune (`git worktree prune`), so that `git worktree list` in the trunk shows only the trunk and the worktree directory no longer exists
criteria.contract: <workspace_root>/<slug>/rebuild/<job id> does not exist afterwards; `git worktree list` in the trunk shows only the trunk; the outcomes are success, conflict result, TransientError, TransientError respectively

setup: a real git repository workspace with an upstream remote and patch branches
a conflicting patch branch for the conflict case
a failure injected for the transient case and a cancelled context for the cancellation case
a mockGitRunner that can inject an error at any step
check.pseudocode:
for scenario in [success, conflict, transient, cancel]: run(scenario); assert !exists(wtPath); assert lines(git('worktree list')) == 1
for step in allSteps+[none,cancel]: run(inject(step)); if mock.added: assert mock.calls.endsWith(['WorktreeRemove','WorktreePrune']) ; assert !exists(path)

criteria.condition: `git worktree remove` fails
criteria.action: fall back to os.RemoveAll(path) followed by `git worktree prune`, log the failure at warning level, and leave the job outcome unchanged
criteria.contract: The job result and status are identical to those of a run whose removal succeeded; a warning log entry naming the slug and path is written; the worktree directory is gone after the fallback

setup: a mockGitRunner whose WorktreeRemove returns an error
a real temp directory standing in for the worktree path
a captured logger
check.pseudocode: r1 = run(removeOK); r2 = run(removeFails); assert r1 == r2; assert warnLogs contains slug and path; assert !exists(path)

criteria.action: run worktree removal and every other cleanup step with a context derived from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) and a timeout of at most two minutes, so cleanup still executes after the job context is cancelled
criteria.contract: ctx.Err() is nil in the cleanup calls; a deadline exists and is no more than two minutes ahead; the worktree removal actually executed

setup: a mockGitRunner that records ctx.Err() and ctx.Deadline() on WorktreeRemove and WorktreePrune
a job context that is cancelled mid-application
check.pseudocode: assert rec.removeCtxErr == nil; assert rec.deadline - now <= 2*time.Minute

criteria.action: provide WorktreeAdd, WorktreeRemove and WorktreePrune on gitcmd.GitRunner, the carrypatch.GitRunner interface, GitRunnerAdapter and mockGitRunner as the only place worktree commands are spelled, and change MergeNoFF to MergeNoFF(ctx, ref, message string) error where an empty message keeps git's default merge message
criteria.contract: the worktree is created, listed, removed and pruned; the merge with a message has that message as the commit subject; the merge with an empty message has git's default message; the interface assertion `var _ GitRunner = (*mockGitRunner)(nil)` compiles

setup: a real temporary git repository with two diverging branches
gitcmd.GitRunner, GitRunnerAdapter and mockGitRunner compiled against the carrypatch.GitRunner interface
check.pseudocode: a.WorktreeAdd(ctx,p,sha); a.WorktreeRemove(ctx,p); a.WorktreePrune(ctx); a.MergeNoFF(ctx,'b',"Merge branch 'b'"); assert subject(HEAD)=="Merge branch 'b'"

criteria.condition: creating the worktree fails
criteria.action: stop the run before applying any patch, leave no directory under rebuild/ for this run, release the guard and emit hub.rebuild.fail
criteria.contract: HandleRebuildJob returns a non-nil error; no integration-ref update or patch bookkeeping has occurred; the trunk HEAD, index and files are unchanged

setup: a mockGitRunner whose WorktreeAdd returns an error
a captured audit sink
a database with patch rows
check.pseudocode: err = run(); assert err != nil; assert mock.calls('UpdateRef')==0; assert !wslock.RebuildActive(slug); assert tryLock(slug)

requirements.title: The trunk is not touched
requirements.rationale: The shared trunk checkout serves clones, sync and merge jobs, so a rebuild must neither move it nor leave state in it.

criteria.action: run no `checkout`, `reset`, `cherry-pick`, `merge` or `rebase` through the trunk runner during a rebuild other than those defined by Exception A and Exception B, never create the _rebuild_temp branch, and not contain the functions currentCheckout, restoreCheckout or preflightCleanup
criteria.contract: the trunk runner records none of checkout, reset, cherry-pick, merge, rebase; the branch _rebuild_temp is never created; the source contains no function currentCheckout, restoreCheckout or preflightCleanup

setup: a mockGitRunner recording trunk commands
no _rebuild_temp branch and the trunk not on the integration branch
the rebuild_executor.go source
check.pseudocode: assert trunk.cmds ∩ {checkout,reset,cherry-pick,merge,rebase}==∅; assert !grep('func (currentCheckout|restoreCheckout|preflightCleanup)')

criteria.action: for any rebuild that ends in success, fail-fast conflict, continue-mode conflict or cancellation, leave the trunk's `git symbolic-ref HEAD`, `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git status --porcelain` output and the contents of a tracked sample file identical to their values before the run, except under Exception A and Exception B
criteria.contract: `git symbolic-ref HEAD` is identical to before; `git rev-parse HEAD` is identical to before; `git status --porcelain` output is identical to before; the sample file bytes are identical to before

setup: a real git workspace whose trunk is checked out on a non-integration branch with a tracked sample file
patch branches including a conflicting one
a real git workspace with a trunk checked out on a branch other than the integration branch
check.pseudocode:
before = snap(trunk); run(scenario); assert snap(trunk) == before
for cfg in gen(): before=snap(trunk); run(cfg); assert snap(trunk)==before

criteria.condition: patch application finishes and phase two begins
criteria.action: force-update the integration branch to the worktree's final HEAD SHA with `git update-ref refs/heads/<integration> <sha>` using the existing UpdateRef method, never using `branch -f` and never checking the integration branch out
criteria.contract: UpdateRef is called on the trunk runner with refs/heads/<integration> and 'abc123'; no `branch -f` or checkout of the integration branch is recorded

setup: a mockGitRunner whose worktree HEAD returns SHA 'abc123'
check.pseudocode: assert mock.calls('UpdateRef')[0] == ('refs/heads/'+integ,'abc123'); assert no call has args ['branch','-f',...]

criteria.condition: phase two holds the workspace lock
criteria.action: read the previous integration head with `rev-parse --verify refs/heads/<integration>` immediately before the ref update and record it as previous_integration_head_sha, leaving it empty when the branch does not exist
criteria.contract: rev-parse --verify refs/heads/<integration> immediately precedes UpdateRef while the lock is held; previous_integration_head_sha is 'old1' in the first case and empty in the second

setup: a mockGitRunner recording call order and lock state
two cases: the integration branch exists at SHA 'old1' and it does not exist
check.pseudocode: assert order == [rev-parse --verify, UpdateRef]; assert lockHeld at both; assert result.prev == 'old1' / ''

criteria.condition: the ref update has been made under the final lock and the trunk's HEAD is the symbolic ref of the integration branch (Exception A)
criteria.action: run `reset --hard HEAD` in the trunk so the index and files match the new tip, and log this at info level; in every other case run no reset in the trunk
criteria.contract: case 1: after the run the trunk's files and index match the new integration tip, `git status --porcelain` is empty, and an info log entry records the reset; case 2: no reset is run in the trunk and the trunk is unchanged

setup: a real git workspace
case 1: the trunk has the integration branch checked out
case 2: the trunk is on another branch
a captured logger
check.pseudocode: case1: assert git(trunk,'rev-parse HEAD')==newTip; assert status==''; assert infoLog('reset'); case2: assert trunkCmds ∩ {reset}==∅

criteria.condition: phase one runs and a local refs/heads/_rebuild_temp exists (Exception B)
criteria.action: delete that branch and log at info level that it was removed
criteria.contract: After the run `git show-ref refs/heads/_rebuild_temp` finds nothing and a log entry with the slug records the removal

setup: a real git workspace whose trunk is on another branch
a local refs/heads/_rebuild_temp
a captured logger
check.pseudocode: run(); assert exitCode(git('show-ref','refs/heads/_rebuild_temp'))!=0; assert infoLog contains slug

criteria.condition: the _rebuild_temp migration runs and the trunk's HEAD is on _rebuild_temp and any cherry-pick, merge or rebase may be in progress
criteria.action: abort any in-progress cherry-pick, merge or rebase on a best-effort basis, then move HEAD with `checkout --force <branch>` where <branch> is workspaceBranch if it exists as a local branch, else the short name of refs/remotes/origin/HEAD if that exists locally, else run `checkout --detach --force` and log a warning, before deleting _rebuild_temp
criteria.contract: the in-progress operation is aborted; variant 1: trunk HEAD is on workspaceBranch; variant 2: trunk HEAD is on the short name of origin/HEAD; variant 3: trunk HEAD is detached and a warning is logged; _rebuild_temp no longer exists in all variants

setup: a real git workspace whose trunk is on _rebuild_temp with an in-progress conflicted cherry-pick
three variants: workspaceBranch exists locally; it is unset but refs/remotes/origin/HEAD resolves to a local branch; neither exists
check.pseudocode: for v in variants: setup(v); run(); assert symbolicRef(trunk)==expected(v); assert !branchExists('_rebuild_temp')

criteria.condition: the `update-ref` of the integration branch fails
criteria.action: stop phase two before any soft-deletion, compaction or push, release the lock, and emit hub.rebuild.fail
criteria.contract: HandleRebuildJob returns a non-nil error; no patch rows are changed by this run; the lock is free afterwards

setup: a mockGitRunner whose UpdateRef fails
a database with merged_upstream and active patches and a PushIntegration spy
check.pseudocode: err=run(); assert err!=nil; assert rowsUnchanged(); assert push.calls==0; assert tryLock(slug)

requirements.title: Rerere across worktrees
requirements.rationale: Conflict resolutions recorded by the hub's rebuilds must keep replaying and stay visible to the rerere endpoints even though patches are applied in a linked worktree.

criteria.action: set rerere.enabled=true and rerere.autoupdate=true in the repository-level config with the trunk runner before creating the worktree, and not enable extensions.worktreeConfig
criteria.contract: config rerere.enabled=true and rerere.autoupdate=true are issued on the trunk runner before WorktreeAdd; no config call mentions extensions.worktreeConfig

setup: a mockGitRunner recording call order
check.pseudocode: assert idx('config rerere.enabled true') < idx('WorktreeAdd'); assert idx('config rerere.autoupdate true') < idx('WorktreeAdd'); assert none(args contains 'worktreeConfig')

criteria.condition: a rebuild meets a conflict whose resolution an earlier rebuild recorded in its worktree
criteria.action: replay the recorded resolution from the shared rr-cache so the patch is applied without a reported conflict
criteria.contract: the conflicting patch is reported as success rather than conflict; the result tree contains the recorded resolution

setup: a real git workspace with two patch branches that conflict on the same hunk
a first rebuild that conflicts, after which the conflict is resolved in its worktree and recorded in rr-cache
check.pseudocode: run1(); resolveAndRecord(); r=run2(); assert r.patch[1].status=='success'

criteria.action: for any resolution recorded in a rebuild worktree, list it in GET /workspaces/:slug/rerere from <trunk>/.git/rr-cache and remove it with DELETE /workspaces/:slug/rerere/*, with the entry absent from a following GET
criteria.contract: the first GET is 200 and lists the entry; DELETE succeeds; the second GET does not list the entry and the rr-cache directory for it is gone from <trunk>/.git/rr-cache

setup: a real workspace with an HTTP router wired to the rerere handlers
one resolution recorded by a rebuild worktree into the common rr-cache
a real workspace and rerere handlers
check.pseudocode:
assert entry in get().entries; assert delete(entry).status==200; assert entry not in get().entries
for set,order in gen(): record(set); for e in order: delete(e); assert get() == set - deleted

criteria.condition: a rebuild worktree is discarded while a conflict is in progress and MERGE_RR is populated
criteria.action: leave the shared rr-cache and the endpoints' read of <trunk>/.git/MERGE_RR unaffected
criteria.contract: GET /workspaces/:slug/rerere returns 200 with the entries recorded before the discard, and <trunk>/.git/MERGE_RR holds no entry from the discarded worktree

setup: a real workspace with one previously recorded resolution
a rebuild that stops on a conflict so MERGE_RR is populated in the worktree
check.pseudocode: assert get().status==200; assert entriesBefore ⊆ get().entries; assert read(trunk/.git/MERGE_RR)==''

requirements.title: Lock phases
requirements.rationale: Only the fetch and the final ref and database update write shared state, so holding the workspace lock for patch application blocks sync, rollback and merge jobs for no benefit.

criteria.condition: a rebuild job starts
criteria.action: resolve upstream credentials first, then take the blocking wslock.Lock(slug), and under that lock call BeginRebuild(slug)
criteria.contract: order is credentials, Lock, BeginRebuild; BeginRebuild observed the lock held

setup: spies for credential resolution, wslock.Lock and BeginRebuild recording order and lock state
check.pseudocode: assert order==['creds','Lock','BeginRebuild']; assert lockHeldDuring(BeginRebuild)

criteria.condition: resolving upstream credentials fails
criteria.action: return a retryable TransientError before taking the lock or setting the guard and emit hub.rebuild.fail
criteria.contract: HandleRebuildJob returns an error of type TransientError; the lock is free and RebuildActive(slug) is false

setup: credential resolution returning an error
a captured audit sink
check.pseudocode: err=run(); var te *TransientError; assert errors.As(err,&te); assert !wslock.RebuildActive(slug); assert tryLock(slug)

criteria.action: perform in phase one under the lock, in this order, the upstream fetch, trunk runner creation, resolveUpstreamBase, the _rebuild_temp migration, stale worktree cleanup and rerere config, and then release the lock
criteria.contract: order is fetch, trunk runner creation, resolveUpstreamBase, _rebuild_temp migration, stale cleanup, rerere config; the lock is held for every step and released before WorktreeAdd

setup: a mock runner and spies recording order and lock state
check.pseudocode: assert order==[fetch,newRunner,resolveBase,migrate,staleCleanup,rerereConfig]; assert allLocked; assert !locked(at WorktreeAdd)

criteria.condition: the rebuild is creating the worktree, listing patches, snapshotting tips or applying patches
criteria.action: hold no wslock lock, so that POST /sync, rollback, rerere forget, batch rebase and merge jobs for the same workspace acquire the lock and proceed
criteria.contract: TryLock(slug) succeeds while blocked; sync responds with its normal success status, not 409 workspace_busy, and updates upstream_head_sha; rollback and rerere forget succeed; the rebuild keeps the base SHA resolved in phase one and completes

setup: a fake runner that blocks inside a cherry-pick until released
real sync, rollback and rerere-forget handlers
the rebuild started in a goroutine
check.pseudocode: go run(); <-blocked; assert tryLock(slug); assert post('/sync').status==200; assert rollback().status==200; assert forget().status==200; release()

criteria.action: re-acquire wslock.Lock(slug) for phase two, perform in it the previous-head read, the integration-ref update, soft-deletion of merged_upstream patches, position compaction and the optional PushIntegration to origin, and release the lock afterwards
criteria.contract: Lock is acquired a second time after patch application; previous-head read, UpdateRef, soft-deletion, compaction and PushIntegration all happen with the lock held in that order; the lock is released afterwards

setup: a mock runner, a PushIntegration spy and a database with merged_upstream patches
check.pseudocode: assert order==[lock,readPrev,updateRef,softDelete,compact,push,unlock]

criteria.action: for any early return in phase one or phase two, release the workspace lock, and perform worktree creation, patch application and worktree removal outside any lock
criteria.contract: tryLock(slug) succeeds after HandleRebuildJob returns; WorktreeAdd, patch application and WorktreeRemove never run while the lock is held

setup: a mock runner that can fail at any step
check.pseudocode: for step in allSteps: run(failAt(step)); assert tryLock(slug); assert !lockedDuring(worktree ops)

criteria.condition: a rollback of the integration branch completes while patches are being applied
criteria.action: overwrite the rolled-back value with its own update-ref in phase two and record in previous_integration_head_sha the value read at phase two, with rollback and the final update serialised by the lock
criteria.contract: After the run the integration branch equals the rebuild's final HEAD SHA and previous_integration_head_sha equals the rolled-back SHA

setup: a real workspace whose integration branch is at SHA 'A'
a rebuild blocked mid-application
a rollback target SHA 'R'
check.pseudocode: rollback('R'); release(); assert rev('integration')==finalSHA; assert result.prev=='R'

criteria.action: after phase two, remove the worktree, run the stale-input check, emit hub.rebuild.complete, end the guard and return, in that order
criteria.contract: order is WorktreeRemove, stale check, hub.rebuild.complete, end guard; RebuildActive(slug) is true until the complete event

setup: spies recording order for WorktreeRemove, stale-input check, audit emit and the end() call
check.pseudocode: assert order==[remove,staleCheck,emit('hub.rebuild.complete'),end]

requirements.title: Rebuild-active guard
requirements.rationale: Archive and reclone delete the directory the worktree lives in, and a mutex that is not held during patch application cannot stop them.

criteria.action: provide BeginRebuild(slug string) (end func(), ok bool) and RebuildActive(slug string) bool as a per-workspace flag independent of the mutex, and clear the flag on process exit because it is held only in memory
criteria.contract: RebuildActive('a') is true after BeginRebuild and Lock/TryLock behaviour is unaffected; RebuildActive('a') is false after the first end(); the second end() does not clear a guard set later by another run

setup: a fresh wslock instance
check.pseudocode: end,ok=BeginRebuild('a'); assert ok&&RebuildActive('a'); assert TryLock('a'); end(); assert !Active; _,ok2=Begin('a'); end(); assert Active('a')

criteria.condition: BeginRebuild is called for a slug whose guard is already set
criteria.action: return ok=false without changing the existing guard, and make the rebuild return a retryable error
criteria.contract: BeginRebuild returns (nil-safe end, false); the existing guard stays set; HandleRebuildJob returns a retryable error and the job is retried by the queue

setup: a guard already set for slug 'a'
check.pseudocode: end,ok=Begin('a'); assert !ok; end(); assert Active('a'); err=run(); assert isTransient(err); assert tryLock('a')

criteria.action: make the end function returned by BeginRebuild idempotent, so a second call leaves a guard set later by another run untouched
hold the guard from before stale worktree cleanup until after worktree removal on every exit path, calling end through defer
criteria.contract: RebuildActive is true at stale cleanup and after WorktreeRemove completes; RebuildActive is false after HandleRebuildJob returns in all scenarios

setup: spies observing RebuildActive at stale cleanup, WorktreeAdd and WorktreeRemove
success, patch-conflict and error scenarios
check.pseudocode: for s in scenarios: run(s); assert activeAt('staleCleanup') && activeAt('afterRemove'); assert !Active(slug)

criteria.condition: an archive request reaches the clone_status == "ready" branch, TryLock succeeds and RebuildActive(slug) is true
criteria.action: release the lock and refuse the request with the existing workspace_busy message
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy; the workspace is not archived and the lock is free

setup: a ready workspace and the real archive handler
wslock guard set via BeginRebuild with the mutex free
check.pseudocode: BeginRebuild(slug); r=archive(); assert r.status==409; assert r.json.error_type=='workspace_busy'; assert !isArchived(slug); assert tryLock(slug)

criteria.condition: a reclone request obtains TryLock and RebuildActive(slug) is true
criteria.action: release the lock and refuse the request with the existing workspace_busy message
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy; the clone directory is untouched and the lock is free

setup: a ready workspace with a trunk directory and the real reclone handler
the guard set and the mutex free
check.pseudocode: BeginRebuild(slug); r=reclone(); assert r.status==409; assert exists(trunk/marker); assert tryLock(slug)

criteria.condition: no rebuild is active for the workspace and the guard has been ended
criteria.action: behave exactly as before this change, so archive and reclone succeed under the same conditions as without the guard
criteria.contract: archive succeeds with its normal success status and the workspace is archived; reclone is accepted with its normal success status

setup: a ready workspace, a guard set then ended with end()
check.pseudocode: end,_=Begin(slug); end(); assert archive().status==200; assert reclone(other).status==202

criteria.condition: the guard is set and the lock is free
criteria.action: not consult the guard and accept their requests
criteria.contract: none of them returns 409 workspace_busy; each returns its normal success status

setup: the guard set for the workspace and the mutex free
real sync, rollback and rerere-forget handlers
check.pseudocode: BeginRebuild(slug); for ep in [sync,rollback,forget]: assert ep().status != 409

requirements.title: Snapshotting patch tips
requirements.rationale: With the lock released during application, branch names can move, so applying fixed SHAs makes the run deterministic and tells the operator exactly what was applied.

criteria.condition: the patch list is sorted and before the first patch is applied
criteria.action: resolve every patch whose status is not merged_upstream, disabled or deleted with `rev-parse --verify refs/heads/<branch>^{commit}` in the trunk runner and use only the resulting SHA for `git log`, cherry-pick and merge from then on
criteria.contract: rev-parse --verify is called only for non-merged_upstream/disabled/deleted patches, on the trunk runner, with refs/heads/<branch>^{commit}; the resolution happens after sorting and before the first patch application; log, cherry-pick and merge arguments contain the snapshot SHA and never the branch name

setup: a mock trunk runner returning SHAs per branch
patches with statuses active, merged_upstream, disabled and deleted
a branch that moves in the mock after the snapshot
check.pseudocode: assert trunk.calls('rev-parse --verify')==activeBranches; assert none(worktree.args contains branchName)

criteria.condition: a patch uses the rebase strategy
criteria.action: list its commits with `git log --reverse --no-merges --right-only --cherry-pick <base>...<snapshot sha>` in the worktree
criteria.contract: the worktree runner receives log --reverse --no-merges --right-only --cherry-pick base1...sha1

setup: a rebase-strategy patch with snapshot SHA 'sha1' and base 'base1'
a mock worktree runner
check.pseudocode: assert worktree.args('log')==['log','--reverse','--no-merges','--right-only','--cherry-pick','base1...sha1']

criteria.condition: a patch uses the merge strategy
criteria.action: call MergeNoFF(ctx, <snapshot sha>, "Merge branch '<branch name>'") in the worktree
criteria.contract: The resulting merge commit message contains the branch name

setup: a real workspace with a merge-strategy patch branch 'feature/x'
check.pseudocode: run(); assert git('log -1 --format=%B integration') contains 'feature/x'

criteria.condition: a patch branch's rev-parse fails or returns empty output, or the rebase strategy yields an empty commit list
criteria.action: record the patch as skipped with reason branch_not_found and continue with the remaining patches
criteria.contract: patch_results contains an entry with status skipped and reason branch_not_found for that patch; the run does not fail because of it

setup: three patches: rev-parse errors, rev-parse returns empty output, and a rebase patch whose log is empty
a fourth healthy patch after them
check.pseudocode: r,err=run(); assert err==nil; assert r.patches[0..2] all skipped/branch_not_found; assert r.patches[3].status=='success'

criteria.condition: a tag or remote-tracking ref has the patch's name but no refs/heads/<branch> exists
criteria.action: treat the branch as not found
criteria.contract: The patch is recorded as skipped with reason branch_not_found

setup: a real workspace where tag 'p1' and refs/remotes/origin/p2 exist but no refs/heads/p1 or refs/heads/p2
check.pseudocode: r=run(); assert r.patches[p1]==('skipped','branch_not_found'); assert r.patches[p2]==('skipped','branch_not_found')

criteria.action: add PatchResult.SourceSHA with JSON name source_sha, omitted when empty, set for every snapshotted patch including those that then conflicted, and carry it in the job result, in the running job's progress and in the patch_results of rebuild API responses
criteria.contract: success and conflict patches carry their snapshot SHA in source_sha; the disabled patch's JSON has no source_sha key; the running job's progress snapshots include source_sha; the API response patch_results include source_sha

setup: a run with one success patch, one conflict patch (continue mode) and one disabled patch
a progress recorder and the rebuild API response encoder
check.pseudocode: assert json(r.patches[0]).source_sha==sha0; assert 'source_sha' not in json(r.patches[2]); assert progress.last.patches[0].source_sha==sha0

criteria.action: for any patch branch that moves after its snapshot, apply exactly the commits reachable from the snapshot SHA and report that SHA as source_sha
criteria.contract: the applied commits equal those reachable from the snapshot SHA only; source_sha equals the snapshot SHA

setup: a real workspace and a rebuild blocked after snapshotting
check.pseudocode: for mv in gen(): snapshot; apply(mv); assert appliedCommits==log(base...snap); assert result.source_sha==snap

requirements.title: Stale-input follow-up
requirements.rationale: Releasing the lock during application lets a push or a sync land mid-run, and without a rebuild-side check the change would never be rebuilt because sync only enqueues when upstream_head_sha changes.

criteria.condition: a run ends in success or in a fail-fast conflict, after worktree removal and after the phase-two lock is released
criteria.action: re-resolve refs/heads/<branch> for each patch with a snapshot SHA and status success or conflict, mark a patch stale if the result differs from its snapshot SHA, ignore patches skipped for merged_upstream, disabled or deleted, and re-run resolveUpstreamBase and mark upstream stale if it differs from the SHA the run used
